title: GSIDI Mentorship Program Fall 2026: Johns Hopkins and AEI Initiative for Prospective Political Science PhD Applicants
summary: Applications are open for the Fall 2026 Graduate Student Intellectual Diversity Initiative Mentorship Program , an initiative designed to support prospective graduate students interested in pursuing PhD study in Political Science, Political Theory, and related areas of academic research . The Graduate Student Intellectual Diversity Initiative (GSIDI) is a joint project led by Steve Teles of the Johns Hopkins University SNF Agora Institute and Jenna Storey of the American Enterprise Institute (AEI) . The initiative seeks to broaden the range of intellectual perspectives represented within higher education by strengthening the pipeline of prospective scholars considering academic careers. For its mentorship program, GSIDI is matching a select group of prospective graduate students with faculty members from leading PhD-granting institutions. Successful applicants will receive individualized guidance during the fall semester as they prepare applications for doctoral study. The initiative is particularly interested in students whose research questions, hypotheses, theoretical perspectives, or approaches may be described as conservative, moderate, or heterodox liberal , as well as applicants interested more broadly in questions of intellectual diversity within academia. Importantly, the initiative does not describe its faculty network as ideologically uniform. According to the program description, participating mentors include scholars from different political perspectives who share an interest in maintaining intellectual diversity within the academic research community. The priority application deadline is September 15, 2026 . About the Graduate Student Intellectual Diversity Initiative The Graduate Student Intellectual Diversity Initiative was created in response to concerns about the range of political and intellectual viewpoints represented within higher education. The initiative argues that when certain perspectives are significantly underrepresented within academic disciplines, this can have consequences for the research process itself. One concern highlighted by GSIDI is what it describes as “field compression.” In this context, field compression refers to a situation where the range of: Research questions being asked Hypotheses being considered Theoretical approaches being used Interpretations being debated Assumptions being questioned may become narrower because certain intellectual or ideological perspectives are less frequently represented within a discipline. GSIDI therefore focuses not only on existing university faculty but on the graduate-school pipeline that produces future academics . The initiative aims to identify promising prospective scholars early in their academic journey and provide them with mentorship before and during the PhD application process. Who Leads GSIDI? The Graduate Student Intellectual Diversity Initiative is jointly led by: Steve Teles Steve Teles is affiliated with the SNF Agora Institute at Johns Hopkins University . Jenna Storey Jenna Storey is affiliated with the American Enterprise Institute . Together, they have developed GSIDI as a program focused on strengthening intellectual diversity within higher education by supporting prospective graduate students. The initiative has initially built a national network of scholars in: Political Science Political Theory The organizers hope that the model may eventually inspire similar efforts in other academic fields, although the current program described in the supplied materials focuses specifically on these areas. What Is the GSIDI Mentorship Program? The GSIDI Mentorship Program matches selected prospective graduate students with established professors at highly ranked PhD-granting institutions. These faculty members have agreed to serve as mentors because of their commitment to intellectual diversity within academic research and graduate education. Successful applicants will receive advice over the course of the fall semester while preparing for graduate-school applications. The program is therefore particularly relevant to students who are: Planning to apply to PhD programs during Fall 2026 Interested in Political Science or Political Theory Considering an academic career Seeking guidance from experienced faculty members Interested in research questions or approaches that may fall outside dominant intellectual perspectives within their field What Mentors Will Help With GSIDI mentors are expected to provide general guidance on several areas of academic development. Graduate School Applications One of the primary purposes of the mentorship is to help students navigate the PhD application process. For prospective doctoral students, applying to graduate school can involve difficult decisions regarding: Which programs to target How to identify faculty fit How to frame research interests How to communicate academic potential How to position an application strategically How to understand differences among departments A mentor who already understands graduate admissions and academic culture can provide valuable perspective during this process. Academic Research Direction Applicants will provide information about their research interests when applying. This allows GSIDI to consider whether a prospective student can be matched with a faculty member whose expertise or academic experience is relevant to the applicant’s goals. Mentorship may help candidates think more carefully about: Research questions Areas of specialization Theoretical approaches Intellectual positioning Long-term academic interests Peer-Reviewed Publications The initiative states that mentors may also provide general advice concerning peer-reviewed publication . For prospective academics, learning how scholarly publishing works can be important even before beginning a doctoral program. Faculty mentors may help applicants better understand: What academic journals are looking for How research develops into publishable work The role of peer review How publication fits into an academic career What kinds of research preparation are useful before beginning a PhD The program description does not indicate that participants are guaranteed publication opportunities. Rather, mentors provide general advice about academic publishing. Careers in Academia GSIDI also provides guidance about the prospects of a career in higher education. Applicants who are considering long-term careers as: University professors Academic researchers Political scientists Political theorists Policy scholars may benefit from realistic conversations with experienced faculty members about the structure of academic careers. This could include discussions about graduate study, publishing, research agendas, academic hiring, and the long-term demands of university research. Who Is the Program Designed For? GSIDI is primarily designed for prospective graduate students who are actively applying to PhD programs . The Fall 2026 application asks whether the applicant is currently applying for graduate school and is specifically aimed at students preparing applications during the fall admissions cycle. The initiative is especially interested in candidates whose academic interests involve questions, hypotheses, or approaches that may be described as: Conservative Moderate Heterodox liberal However, this does not mean applicants must adopt a particular political identity. The initiative’s language focuses primarily on intellectual approaches and research questions , rather than requiring applicants to identify personally with a specific political party or ideology. Political Science and Political Theory Focus The current GSIDI network has been launched primarily within: Political Science and: Political Theory The mentorship program connects prospective graduate students with professors at leading doctoral programs in these areas. Applicants planning PhD research in adjacent fields should carefully consider whether their proposed doctoral work fits clearly within Political Science, Political Theory, or the participating scholars’ areas of expertise. The supplied information does not state that the Fall 2026 mentorship program is currently open across all humanities and social-science disciplines. Why GSIDI Focuses on Intellectual Diversity The initiative is based on the view that academic research benefits when scholars approach questions from different intellectual traditions. GSIDI argues that limited representation of center-right and other less common perspectives within some areas of higher education may narrow scholarly debate. From the initiative’s perspective, improving intellectual diversity can increase the range of: Questions researchers ask Explanations scholars test Competing hypotheses considered Interpretive frameworks employed Scholarly disagreements represented The program therefore approaches intellectual diversity as an issue affecting both university culture and the research process. Prospective applicants should understand this intellectual mission before applying and should be able to explain why the program is relevant to their own research interests. Faculty Mentors Successful applicants will be matched with faculty mentors from highly ranked PhD-granting institutions. The initiative emphasizes that participating mentors are established scholars within Political Science and Political Theory. Faculty participating in the network do not necessarily share the same political outlook. Some may be conservative, while others may have liberal or other perspectives but support the principle that academic research should include a wider variety of intellectual viewpoints. This is an important feature of the initiative: the mentorship is not described simply as ideological networking, but as an effort to connect prospective scholars with established academics committed to intellectual diversity. How the Mentorship Works The mentorship is intended to take place over the Fall 2026 semester . The general process is: Prospective PhD applicants complete the GSIDI mentorship application. Applicants provide information about their academic background and research interests. Applicants upload their university transcript. GSIDI staff review the submitted materials. Selected applicants are matched with appropriate faculty mentors. Mentors provide advice as applicants prepare graduate-school applications during the fall. The program description does not specify an exact number of mentorship meetings or a fixed number of hours participants will receive. Applicants should therefore treat the mentorship as individualized academic guidance rather than a standardized course with a predetermined weekly schedule. Application Requirements The application appears intentionally straightforward compared with many fellowship or graduate-admissions applications. Applicants are asked to provide information concerning their: Academic background Research interests Graduate-school plans They must also upload: A copy of their university transcript The program states that submitted materials will only be shared with: GSIDI staff Potential faculty mentors Applicants should carefully complete the form so that organizers have sufficient information to identify an appropriate mentor. University Transcript Applicants must upload their university transcript as part of the application. The information provided does not specify: Whether an official transcript is required Whether an unofficial transcript is acceptable A minimum GPA A particular degree classification Applicants should therefore follow the instructions shown within the official application form. Research Interests Applicants will be asked to provide information about their research interests. This is likely to be particularly important for mentor matching. Candidates should be prepared to explain clearly: What area of Political Science or Political Theory interests them What research questions they may want to investigate Why those questions matter What intellectual or theoretical approaches interest them What type of PhD program they hope to enter A focused description can make it easier for GSIDI staff to understand where the applicant might benefit most from mentorship. Applicants Should Be Preparing for PhD Applications The program is not presented as a general undergraduate mentoring initiative. The Fall 2026 call specifically asks for students who are currently applying to graduate school . Applicants should therefore ideally be at the stage where they are preparing applications for PhD study during the upcoming admissions cycle. This may involve activities such as: Researching doctoral programs Identifying potential supervisors Preparing statements of purpose Developing research interests Requesting recommendation letters Preparing academic writing samples Reviewing transcripts Considering future academic careers Priority Application Deadline The priority deadline is September 15, 2026 . Applicants should distinguish between a priority deadline and a final deadline. The information provided specifies September 15 as the priority deadline but does not state a separate final closing date. Candidates interested in the mentorship should therefore aim to submit their application by September 15, 2026 rather than assuming applications will remain open substantially later. How to Apply Prospective applicants should complete the official Fall 2026 GSIDI Mentorship Application . The application asks candidates to provide details about their research background and academic interests and to upload a university transcript. Information about the broader Graduate Student Intellectual Diversity Initiative is available through the Johns Hopkins University SNF Agora Institute website. If you would like to receive updates about GSIDI news and events, please register HERE . APPLY HERE Questions About the Program Applicants with questions can contact: Jacob Bruggeman Email: Jbrugge2@jhu.edu Prospective candidates may wish to contact the program if they are uncertain about whether their research area fits the current Political Science and Political Theory network. GSIDI News and Events Individuals who are interested in the initiative but are not yet applying to graduate school can also register to receive news and event updates. This could be useful for: Undergraduate students considering future graduate study Master s students planning to apply in a later cycle Researchers interested in intellectual diversity Students interested in academic careers The updates form is separate from the formal mentorship application. Tips for Preparing a Strong GSIDI Application 1. Explain Your Research Interests Clearly Avoid describing your interests only in extremely broad terms such as “politics” or “democracy.” Explain the questions you are actually curious about. For example, identify: A political institution A theoretical problem A policy question A historical development A research puzzle A methodological challenge that you may want to investigate. 2. Explain Why Intellectual Diversity Matters to Your Research The initiative has a distinctive mission. Applicants should therefore be able to explain why GSIDI’s emphasis on intellectual diversity is relevant to them. The strongest explanation need not be ideological. It could focus on: Testing competing hypotheses Challenging assumptions Engaging opposing arguments Expanding theoretical perspectives Improving research design Encouraging more rigorous debate 3. Avoid Treating Political Identity as the Entire Application The initiative focuses on broadening intellectual perspectives, but applicants are still applying for academic mentorship . A strong application should therefore demonstrate: Serious research interests Academic preparation Intellectual curiosity Interest in doctoral study Potential for scholarly development Political self-identification alone is unlikely to communicate sufficient academic potential. 4. Be Specific About Your PhD Plans Explain where you are in the application process. You may want to identify: General subfield Research topics Types of programs Career objectives This can help GSIDI determine which faculty mentor may be most useful. 5. Prepare Your Transcript Early Because the application requires a university transcript, obtain the appropriate document before beginning the final submission process. 6. Apply by the Priority Deadline Aim for: September 15, 2026 rather than waiting to see whether applications remain open afterward. Why This Mentorship Can Be Valuable PhD admissions differ considerably from undergraduate and many master s admissions processes. Applicants are often evaluated not only on grades but on: Intellectual potential Research fit Academic writing Research experience Recommendation letters Clarity of scholarly goals Fit with faculty and departments For students unfamiliar with academic institutions, understanding these expectations can be difficult. A faculty mentor with experience in leading Political Science or Political Theory programs may help prospective applicants better understand how academic departments evaluate doctoral candidates. The mentorship can also help students think beyond admission itself and consider whether a long-term career in academic research is genuinely appropriate for their goals. What the Program Does Not Promise Based on the information provided, GSIDI should not be described as guaranteeing: Admission to a PhD program Funding for doctoral study A scholarship A paid stipend Employment Publication Placement at a specific university Its central benefit is faculty mentorship and guidance . Applicants should therefore understand it primarily as an academic-development and PhD-application mentorship opportunity. Important Information at a Glance Program: Graduate Student Intellectual Diversity Initiative Mentorship Program Cycle: Fall 2026 Academic areas: Political Science and Political Theory Organizers: Johns Hopkins University SNF Agora Institute and American Enterprise Institute-affiliated project leadership Program leaders: Steve Teles and Jenna Storey Target group: Prospective graduate students applying for PhD programs Main activity: Faculty mentorship during the PhD application process Mentor network: Professors at highly ranked PhD-granting institutions Application materials: Background information, research interests, and university transcript Priority deadline: September 15, 2026 Contact: Jbrugge2@jhu.edu Conclusion The Graduate Student Intellectual Diversity Initiative Mentorship Program Fall 2026 offers a distinctive opportunity for prospective Political Science and Political Theory PhD applicants seeking individualized guidance from established academics. Led jointly by Steve Teles of the Johns Hopkins University SNF Agora Institute and Jenna Storey of the American Enterprise Institute, GSIDI seeks to strengthen intellectual diversity in higher education by focusing on the pipeline through which future university researchers and professors are trained. Selected participants will be matched with faculty mentors from leading PhD-granting institutions and receive guidance during the fall graduate-school application cycle. Mentors may advise participants on: PhD applications Academic research Peer-reviewed publications Graduate-school strategy Careers in academia The program is particularly intended for prospective scholars whose research questions, hypotheses, or approaches may be characterized as conservative, moderate, or heterodox liberal, although the faculty network itself includes scholars with different political viewpoints who share an interest in intellectual diversity. Applicants should be preparing to apply to PhD programs during Fall 2026 and should be ready to provide information about their research interests, academic background, and university transcript. The priority deadline is September 15, 2026 . For students considering a future in Political Science or Political Theory who want experienced academic guidance before submitting doctoral applications, GSIDI provides an opportunity to receive targeted mentorship during a particularly important stage of the academic career pipeline. title: INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme 2026: Applications Open for Law Enforcement Officers and Criminal Investigation Experts Worldwide
summary: The International Criminal Police Organization, better known as INTERPOL, has opened applications for its Enhanced Secondment Programme , a major international professional opportunity designed to strengthen global law enforcement cooperation by bringing qualified police officers, law enforcement specialists and government officials from INTERPOL Member Countries into its international operational environment. The programme provides an opportunity for experienced law enforcement professionals to contribute their expertise to international efforts against transnational crime while gaining exposure to complex international policing operations, investigative techniques, advanced technologies and multinational cooperation. The opportunity is based within INTERPOL s operational structures, with the vacancy announcement indicating multiple duty stations and a secondment duration of 36 months . The programme is associated with Grade 5 positions and requires candidates to meet INTERPOL s eligibility, professional experience, endorsement and security requirements. According to the vacancy notice, the programme is intended to create a dynamic and secure pool of vetted law enforcement specialists who can be deployed or assigned according to operational needs, ensuring that the right expertise is available to address international crime challenges. About the INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme INTERPOL is the world s largest international police organization, with 196 member states . Established in 1923, the organization facilitates cross-border police cooperation and supports authorities and organizations whose missions involve preventing and combating international crime. Through the Enhanced Secondment Programme, INTERPOL is seeking qualified law enforcement officers and experts who can strengthen its global operational capabilities and help the organization provide high-quality services to Member Countries. The programme is particularly relevant to professionals whose careers involve criminal investigations, intelligence analysis, cybercrime, financial crime, border security, organized crime, environmental crime, counter-terrorism, forensics, operational coordination, training, information management and other specialized law enforcement functions. The vacancy notice identifies the position as the INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Program , reporting to coordinators within operational directorates. Although the vacancy page identifies Lyon, France as the location of the published opportunity, the detailed vacancy information specifies multiple duty stations , reflecting the international and operational nature of the programme. Key Details of the Opportunity Opportunity: INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme Organization: INTERPOL Vacancy Notice: 1663 Publication starting date: August 2, 2026 Location indicated on the vacancy page: Lyon, France Duty stations: Multiple duty stations Duration: 36 months Grade: Grade 5 Security clearance: Basic/Enhanced Application deadline: Applications are received throughout the year Eligible applicants: Qualified law enforcement and governmental officials from INTERPOL Member Countries Application route: INTERPOL Recruitment Hub through the organization s vacancies page Endorsement: Applications must be officially endorsed and submitted through the relevant National Central Bureau (NCB). What Is the Objective of the INTERPOL Secondment Programme? The programme aims to establish a pool of vetted law enforcement specialists capable of supporting INTERPOL s international operational requirements. The objective is to maintain a dynamic, secure and interoperable global repository of specialists who can provide the right expertise at the right time in response to international crime and policing challenges. This approach enables INTERPOL to strengthen cooperation between Member Countries and improve its ability to coordinate responses to transnational criminal activity. For participating officers, the programme can also provide exposure to an international working environment where professionals from different national law enforcement systems work together on shared security and criminal justice challenges. Who Can Apply? The Enhanced Secondment Programme is specifically targeted at professionals already working within law enforcement and government structures in INTERPOL Member Countries. Eligible categories identified in the vacancy include: Active police officers Serving police officers can apply where their professional experience and specialization correspond to the operational areas sought by INTERPOL. Law enforcement officers from national agencies This includes professionals working in agencies such as customs, border control and anti-corruption units, as well as other national law enforcement bodies. Civil servants working in law enforcement or government administrations Government officials whose responsibilities are directly connected to law enforcement or relevant national government functions may also be considered. The vacancy specifically states that the announcement applies to law enforcement and/or governmental officials within INTERPOL Member Countries. Areas of Expertise Sought The Enhanced Secondment Programme covers a broad range of criminal justice, policing and operational specialties. Prospective candidates may be considered for different Grade 5 operational positions depending on their professional background and expertise. Examples include: Criminal Intelligence Officer Professionals in this area may contribute to the analysis and dissemination of intelligence concerning transnational crime and support international efforts to identify and respond to criminal threats. Specialized Officer Specialized officers may work on particular crime types or specialist operational areas, including fugitives, disaster victim identification, cybercrime, human trafficking and financial crime. Regional Specialized Officer These professionals support regional operations by bringing localized knowledge and expertise relevant to particular geographical or operational environments. Criminal Intelligence Analyst Criminal intelligence analysts may collect, analyze and interpret criminal-related data and activities while supporting crime prevention and investigative operations. Crime Areas Covered by the Programme INTERPOL has identified a broad, non-exhaustive list of crime areas and policing capabilities that candidates can select as areas of interest within their applications. 1. Financial Crimes Relevant areas include: Anti-corruption Money laundering and asset recovery Fraud and financial crimes Counterfeit currency and security documents These areas are increasingly important in international law enforcement because financial investigations can reveal criminal networks operating across multiple jurisdictions. 2. Cyber and Digital Forensics The programme also covers emerging digital crime areas such as: Cybercrime Darknet investigations Cryptocurrency tracing Ransomware analysis Artificial intelligence fraud detection Professionals with specialized digital investigation and cyber-forensics experience can therefore find their expertise relevant to the programme. 3. Transnational and Organized Crime This broad category includes: Human trafficking and smuggling networks Online crimes against children War crimes and illicit arms Vehicle crime Drug trafficking Works of art Illicit goods and global health Intellectual property crime and digital piracy Public health and pharmaceutical crime These areas reflect the international nature of modern organized crime and the need for law enforcement agencies to collaborate across borders. 4. Environmental Crime Applicants with expertise in environmental enforcement may have experience in: Wildlife crime Fisheries crime Forestry crime Pollution Illegal mining Environmental crime can involve sophisticated cross-border networks, making international cooperation particularly important. 5. Counter-Terrorism and Extremism Relevant expertise includes: Counter-terrorism Chemical and explosives terrorism prevention Radiological and nuclear terrorism prevention Bioterrorism prevention Candidates working in these specialized security areas may therefore find the programme aligned with their professional expertise. 6. Forensics and Bio-Crime The vacancy identifies several forensic and identification-related areas, including: DNA analysis Biometrics Disaster victim identification Fingerprints and facial recognition Border control Counterfeit currency and security documents These capabilities can play an important role in international criminal investigations and identification processes. 7. Capacity Building and Training Professionals with experience in training and institutional development may be considered in areas such as: Training and development Digital curriculum design and operations This reflects INTERPOL s emphasis not only on operational investigations but also on strengthening the capabilities of law enforcement institutions. 8. Command and Coordination The programme also includes expertise in: Operations coordination, planning and support Communication assistance and information management Critical regional operations languages Professionals in these areas can contribute to coordination between different operational teams and Member Countries. 9. Global Outreach and Regional Assistance Candidates with experience in international or regional coordination may contribute to: Coordination of regional activities Support to National Central Bureaus This area is particularly relevant to professionals experienced in working with multiple institutions and stakeholders across jurisdictions. 10. Criminal Intelligence Analysis and Fusion The programme also seeks expertise in: Collection, analysis and interpretation of criminal-related data and activities Open-source intelligence and analysis These skills are increasingly important as law enforcement agencies deal with large amounts of structured and unstructured information originating from multiple sources. Main Duties and Responsibilities Successful seconded officers will be expected to contribute to INTERPOL s operational objectives under the supervision and guidance of management. The responsibilities are designed around addressing specific crime phenomena and supporting coordination of criminal cases and business continuity within existing activities. Key duties include: Coordinating investigations and cases between Member Countries. Identifying, establishing and maintaining professional contact with experts in relevant fields. Organizing and participating in training programmes. Participating in expert group meetings and conferences. Monitoring and analyzing information relating to the assigned area of activity. Developing remedies and best-practice solutions to challenges affecting the effectiveness of law enforcement agencies. Identifying major criminal threats with potential global impact. Developing strategic partnerships with national, sub-regional, regional and global organizations. Serving as a point of contact for Member Countries seeking assistance or advice in the relevant area. Carrying out other responsibilities assigned by the supervisor or organizational hierarchy. The programme therefore requires candidates who can combine technical or investigative expertise with communication, coordination, analysis and international cooperation skills. Education and Academic Requirements Candidates are expected to have three to four years of university-level study or other specialized higher education . The vacancy indicates that academic backgrounds in the following areas are particularly relevant: Law Public policy Police management Related disciplines Equivalent legal or police academy qualifications may also be considered. Importantly, the vacancy provides an alternative pathway for candidates who do not possess the required educational qualifications. Such candidates must demonstrate 10 years of relevant professional experience . Professional Experience Requirements Applicants should have substantial practical experience relevant to law enforcement and criminal investigations. The vacancy requires: At least three years of hands-on experience in police operations or criminal investigations. Specialization in one or more areas of transnational crime. Extensive experience as a law enforcement officer. A strong background in specialized criminal investigations. Regional, sub-regional and/or national operational police support experience. International experience is highly desirable, particularly experience gained through employment with an international organization, participation in international working groups or involvement in joint international projects. Applicants should therefore carefully match their professional experience with the crime areas and operational functions identified by INTERPOL. Language Requirements Professional fluency in English is required , including both written and oral communication. Knowledge of additional languages is considered an asset. The vacancy specifically identifies: French Spanish Arabic Other languages as useful additional language capabilities. Given the international environment in which INTERPOL operates, strong communication skills can be particularly important for professionals who will coordinate with colleagues, experts and authorities from different countries. Additional Skills Required In addition to academic and professional qualifications, applicants should demonstrate relevant technical and professional skills. The vacancy identifies: Sound investigative skills Strong written communication skills Strong oral communication skills Public speaking ability Presentation and briefing skills Computer literacy Familiarity with presentation software Knowledge of business intelligence software Knowledge of word-processing software These skills complement the technical law enforcement experience required for the programme. National Central Bureau Endorsement Is Essential One of the most important aspects of the application process is the requirement for official endorsement through the applicant s National Central Bureau (NCB) . Candidates are required to: Complete their application online through the INTERPOL Recruitment Hub. Submit the completed application together with a Support Letter or Letter of Nomination from their respective NCB. Candidates working in non-police law enforcement agencies should coordinate with their designated NCB before submitting their application. Ensure that the application is endorsed and submitted through the NCB. The vacancy clearly states that only applications endorsed and submitted through the NCB will be considered. Applicants should therefore not treat the NCB endorsement as an optional administrative step. It is a central component of the application process. Secondment Financial and Administrative Arrangements Prospective applicants should also understand that the secondment arrangement places several financial and administrative responsibilities on the officer s home administration, agency, service or government. According to the vacancy notice, the home administration or government is responsible for the officer s: Salary or remuneration Social insurance Pension contributions Welfare benefits Family allowances Benefits during the assignment Travel expenses Removal expenses associated with arrival and departure Other related costs depending on the circumstances Candidates are required to obtain written confirmation from their home administration, agency, service or government that it agrees to the applicable Conditions of Secondment. This confirmation should then be forwarded to INTERPOL through the relevant NCB. Applicants should therefore consult the applicable Conditions of Secondment and engage their relevant national authorities before proceeding too far with the application. Professional Development and Career Growth The programme can provide participating officers with valuable exposure to international law enforcement cooperation and professional development. The vacancy identifies several professional development opportunities associated with secondment, including: Greater awareness of complex international working environments. Development of cultural bridges and cross-border professional relationships. Advancement of policing, investigative and operational coordination skills. Exposure to cutting-edge technologies. Opportunities to pursue an international career. Opportunities for professional growth. Membership in a global network of law enforcement experts. INTERPOL also indicates that career progression may be possible through its learning and training activities. Successful experience in an Officer role, combined with relevant leadership development, could potentially lead to mid-executive positions such as: Coordinator or Operations Coordinator at Grade 4. Senior Coordinator or Senior Operations Coordinator at Grade 3. Diversity and Inclusion INTERPOL states that it aims to maintain a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcomes applications from people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. The organization particularly welcomes applications from women and nationals of underrepresented or unrepresented Member Countries . However, recruitment remains merit-based, meaning that hiring decisions are based on candidates qualifications and the operational needs of the organization. Application Deadline There is no fixed closing date stated for this opportunity . The vacancy specifies: Deadline: Applications received throughout the year. However, applicants should not interpret this as a reason to delay preparation. Because the programme involves NCB endorsement, government approval and supporting documentation, eligible professionals should begin the process early enough to obtain the necessary institutional support. How to Apply Applications should be submitted online through the Vacancies section of INTERPOL s recruitment platform. The vacancy specifically directs candidates to use the recruitment page and emphasizes that applications must be endorsed and submitted through the appropriate National Central Bureau. Before applying, candidates should: Review the Conditions of Secondment applicable to the programme. Confirm their eligibility based on their law enforcement or government status. Identify the crime area or specialist field that best matches their professional experience. Prepare a detailed and accurate application highlighting relevant operational experience. Contact and coordinate with the relevant National Central Bureau. Obtain the required Support Letter or Letter of Nomination. Secure written confirmation from the home administration regarding the Conditions of Secondment and associated responsibilities. Complete the online application through the INTERPOL recruitment system. Ensure the application is formally endorsed and submitted through the NCB. The official INTERPOL website provides access to the organization s recruitment and career information. APPLY HERE What Applicants Should Emphasize in Their Applications Because the programme is highly specialized, applicants should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates how their professional background corresponds with INTERPOL s operational needs. Strong applications should clearly explain relevant experience in areas such as: Criminal investigations Transnational crime Criminal intelligence Cybercrime and digital investigations Financial investigations Counter-terrorism Human trafficking Drug trafficking Border control Forensics Wildlife and environmental crime Intelligence analysis International police cooperation Operations coordination Training and capacity building Information management Open-source intelligence Candidates should avoid submitting generic descriptions of their professional duties. Instead, they should demonstrate their actual responsibilities, specialized expertise, operational exposure and experience working with other agencies or jurisdictions. Where applicable, applicants should also highlight experience in international working groups, cross-border investigations, joint operations, international conferences, regional initiatives and collaborative projects. Why the INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme Is Significant The programme comes at a time when criminal networks increasingly operate across national borders and exploit technology, financial systems, transportation networks and digital platforms. Effective responses therefore require law enforcement agencies to share intelligence, coordinate investigations and develop common approaches to emerging threats. The Enhanced Secondment Programme provides a mechanism through which experienced national law enforcement professionals can contribute their expertise within an international policing environment while strengthening their own professional knowledge and networks. The programme s broad coverage of financial crime, cybercrime, organized crime, environmental crime, terrorism, forensics, intelligence, training and operational coordination also demonstrates the wide range of expertise required to address modern transnational crime. Visit HERE for more information about the INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme 2026. Conclusion The INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme 2026 presents a significant international professional opportunity for qualified police officers, law enforcement specialists and relevant government officials from INTERPOL Member Countries. With a stated 36-month duration , Grade 5 classification and multiple operational areas, the programme is designed to strengthen INTERPOL s global operational capacity while giving participating professionals the opportunity to work within an international law enforcement environment. The opportunity is particularly relevant to professionals with strong backgrounds in criminal investigations, police operations, intelligence, cybercrime, financial crime, organized crime, counter-terrorism, forensics, environmental crime, border control, training, information management and operational coordination. Applicants should pay particular attention to the NCB endorsement requirement , the Conditions of Secondment and the financial responsibilities of their home administration. They should also ensure that their academic qualifications, professional experience, language abilities and specialist expertise are clearly aligned with the requirements outlined in the vacancy. Since applications are accepted throughout the year , there is no single fixed application deadline. Nevertheless, eligible professionals are encouraged to begin the process early, particularly because obtaining institutional endorsement and the required documentation may take time. For qualified law enforcement and governmental professionals seeking international exposure, specialized professional development and the opportunity to contribute to global efforts against transnational crime, the INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme offers a potentially valuable pathway into international law enforcement cooperation. title: British Council International Consultant for Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) in Sudan 2026: Application Guide, Requirements and Deadline
summary: The British Council is seeking an International Consultant or Consultancy Firm for the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) initiative in Sudan , offering an important opportunity for experienced education, skills-development and policy professionals to contribute to the development of a comprehensive national framework designed to recognise skills acquired through formal, non-formal and informal pathways. The consultancy will provide technical support for the development of a National Recognition of Prior Learning Policy Framework in Sudan , with particular attention to Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), Non-Formal Education (NFE), higher education, qualifications, assessment, certification, institutional governance and quality assurance. Applications for the consultancy close on 26 August 2026 . The successful consultant or consultancy firm will be expected to provide technical leadership and work with national stakeholders and development partners to develop a comprehensive, cross-sectoral National RPL Policy Framework that is operational, implementable and ready for government endorsement. About the British Council International RPL Consultancy in Sudan The British Council is implementing this initiative through its Youth Skills Programme in Sudan , which is supporting system-level reforms within Technical and Vocational Education and Training and Non-Formal Education. The broader objective is to improve young people s access to employment and lifelong learning opportunities. The need for a Recognition of Prior Learning system is particularly significant within the Sudanese context. Ongoing conflict and displacement mean that a considerable amount of skills acquisition takes place through informal and non-formal channels. People may develop valuable competencies through work, community activities, informal training, apprenticeships and other experiences without necessarily receiving formal qualifications recognising what they have learned. When such competencies remain unrecognised by formal education and training systems, individuals can face difficulties progressing into further education or securing employment that appropriately reflects their capabilities. The British Council initiative therefore seeks to help address the gap between skills acquired outside conventional formal education and the qualifications and recognition available through established systems. Background to the Recognition of Prior Learning Initiative The consultancy does not begin from scratch. It builds on earlier policy work and stakeholder engagement concerning Recognition of Prior Learning in Sudan. In March 2026 , the British Council convened a national Policy Dialogue on Recognition of Prior Learning. The dialogue brought together stakeholders including: Ministry of Education; Ministry of Higher Education; Ministry of Labour; Supreme Council for Vocational Training and Apprenticeship; National Centre for Curriculum and Educational Research; Private-sector representatives; Trade unions; Civil society organisations; and Development partners. The national dialogue produced two particularly important outputs. The first was a Policy Brief outlining key principles and system components required for Recognition of Prior Learning. The second was a Roadmap identifying phased steps for designing and implementing an RPL system. The Policy Brief identified critical areas such as regulatory frameworks, institutional arrangements, financing, quality assurance and stakeholder engagement. Meanwhile, the Roadmap established a phased pathway covering system design, implementation and continuous improvement. The new consultancy is intended to build upon these foundations and move the process towards a comprehensive National RPL Policy Framework that can ultimately be considered for government endorsement. Why the National RPL Framework Is Important for Sudan Sudan s political, economic and humanitarian circumstances have placed considerable pressure on the country s skills system and labour market. Conflict has disrupted education, contributed to widespread displacement and severely constrained or rendered non-operational parts of the education system. At the same time, young people represent a substantial proportion of Sudan s population, while unemployment remains high and the informal economy plays a dominant role. These circumstances create significant challenges for young people attempting to enter skilled, sustainable employment. Sectors with potential for economic growth require workers equipped with practical competencies and professional skills. However, disruption to education and limited access to quality learning have increased the importance of developing a skills system that is responsive, inclusive and resilient. A well-designed Recognition of Prior Learning framework could help create mechanisms through which existing competencies can be assessed, recognised and potentially connected with qualifications, further learning and employment pathways. Programmes Supporting the Initiative The activity forms part of the British Council s Going Global Partnerships (GGP) and Youth Connect programmes in Sudan. Going Global Partnerships supports mutually beneficial higher education and TVET collaboration between the United Kingdom and other countries. The programme aims to contribute to stronger, more inclusive and globally connected tertiary systems capable of supporting economic and social growth. Youth Connect, meanwhile, supports young people in developing the skills, confidence, inspiration and connections required to address major challenges including employability, inequality, conflict and climate change. The RPL consultancy therefore sits within a broader effort to strengthen education, skills development and opportunities for young people. Purpose of the British Council RPL Consultancy The British Council intends to appoint an individual consultant or consultancy firm capable of providing technical guidance and support to Sudan s TVET and Non-Formal Education systems. A central responsibility will be the development of a National Recognition of Prior Learning Policy Framework aligned with Sudan s TVET, NFE and higher education systems. The assignment is expected to ensure that the resulting framework supports both horizontal and vertical mobility between non-formal, technical and academic pathways. This is important because an effective RPL system should not merely acknowledge previously acquired competencies. It should also help establish pathways through which recognised learning can support progression between different parts of the education, training and qualifications system. The consultant or firm must consequently work towards an operational and implementable framework covering areas such as: Governance; Assessment; Certification; Quality assurance; Institutional responsibilities; Policy and legal provisions; Qualifications; Mobility between learning pathways; and Practical implementation. The consultant will also facilitate a co-creation process involving national stakeholders and development partners to strengthen national ownership and prepare the framework for endorsement. Scope of Work for the International RPL Consultant The consultancy involves an extensive scope of work covering policy design, institutional governance, assessment, certification, quality assurance, implementation, stakeholder consultation and endorsement support. 1. System Design and Policy Development The consultant or consultancy firm will begin by reviewing and consolidating the existing RPL Policy Brief and Roadmap. The assignment will require analysis of Sudan s existing: Legal landscape; Institutional environment; and Qualifications landscape. Using this analysis and the existing policy work, the consultant will design a comprehensive National Recognition of Prior Learning Policy Framework. The framework is expected to address: Policy provisions; Legal provisions; Integration with national qualifications frameworks; and Cross-sectoral articulation involving TVET, Non-Formal Education and higher education. This component is fundamental because the RPL system must be connected to Sudan s broader education, training and qualifications architecture rather than operating as an isolated mechanism. 2. Institutional Architecture and Governance A national RPL system requires clearly defined institutional responsibilities. The consultant will therefore define the roles and responsibilities of relevant institutions and stakeholder groups, including: Ministry of Education; Ministry of Higher Education; Ministry of Labour; Supreme Council for Vocational Training and Apprenticeship; National Centre for Curriculum and Educational Research; Training providers; Employers; and Civil society organisations. The consultant will also propose an appropriate national governance model. This is expected to cover matters including: Coordination mechanisms; Oversight structures; Implementation responsibilities; and Institutional arrangements required for effective administration of the RPL system. Recommendations may also involve establishing new RPL units or mechanisms or strengthening existing institutional structures where appropriate. 3. Competency-Based Assessment and Certification Model Another major component of the consultancy concerns the way people s existing competencies will actually be assessed and formally recognised. The consultant will develop a competency-based RPL assessment framework . Potential assessment methodologies specifically identified within the assignment include: Portfolios; Practical tests; and Interviews. The framework must also address certification pathways and equivalency mechanisms. Additionally, the consultant will consider credit transfer and articulation systems , helping establish how recognised competencies could contribute towards qualifications or progression between different education and training pathways. 4. National RPL Quality Assurance Framework Recognition will only have meaningful long-term value if institutions, employers, learners and other stakeholders can have confidence in the quality and consistency of the system. The consultant will therefore design a national quality assurance system for RPL. This will include: National standards; Guidelines; Accreditation mechanisms; Monitoring arrangements; Evaluation processes; and Continuous improvement mechanisms. The quality assurance framework will be important in supporting consistency, credibility and sustainability across the wider RPL system. 5. RPL Implementation Guidelines and Operational Manual The assignment extends beyond high-level policy development. The British Council requires a framework capable of being implemented in practice. The consultant will therefore develop a detailed Operational Manual . The manual is expected to provide guidance concerning: Step-by-step implementation processes; Institutional workflows; Roles and responsibilities of assessors; Roles and responsibilities of institutions; and Learner support mechanisms. Learner support is expected to include areas such as: Guidance; Counselling; and Bridging mechanisms. This operational dimension is particularly important because it translates national policy into procedures that institutions and practitioners can actually follow. 6. Stakeholder Engagement and Co-Creation Stakeholder participation is a central component of the assignment. The consultant or consultancy firm will facilitate a structured consultation process involving a broad range of stakeholders. Government stakeholders are expected to include the relevant bodies responsible for education, higher education, labour, vocational training and curriculum development. Consultations will also involve: Private-sector organisations; Employers; Civil society organisations; Training providers; and Development partners. Development partners specifically identified in the Terms of Reference include organisations such as: International Labour Organization; UNESCO; Norwegian Refugee Council; and International Organization for Migration. Workshops will be conducted using in-person and/or hybrid formats to validate key elements of the proposed framework. This collaborative approach is intended to ensure that the resulting RPL framework reflects national realities, incorporates stakeholder expertise and develops sufficient ownership to support implementation and endorsement. 7. Finalisation and Government Endorsement Support After consultation, the consultant will incorporate relevant stakeholder feedback into the final framework. The consultant will also support the preparation of documentation suitable for endorsement and provide technical input for high-level validation or endorsement meetings. Consequently, the assignment covers the development process from policy analysis and system design through stakeholder consultation and final preparation for potential government endorsement. Expected Deliverables The consultant or consultancy firm will be responsible for producing a substantial set of deliverables. These include: Inception Report covering the methodology, workplan and stakeholder engagement plan. Draft National RPL Policy Framework . Institutional Architecture and Governance Model . Assessment and Certification Framework . Quality Assurance Framework . RPL Implementation Guidelines / Operational Manual . Consultation Reports summarising stakeholder contributions and inputs. Final National RPL Policy Framework , prepared in an endorsement-ready format. These deliverables demonstrate that the assignment requires expertise spanning policy development, technical design, institutional analysis, stakeholder engagement and practical implementation planning. Duration of the Consultancy The consultancy will run from contract signature until 31 March 2027 . Rather than being completed as a single continuous exercise, the work is expected to be organised around phased milestones aligned with stakeholder consultation and validation processes. The assignment has an estimated level of effort of up to 42 working days , distributed throughout the contract period. Those working days are intended to cover major deliverables, consultation activities and reporting responsibilities. Travel, Workshops and Operational Support Additional operational budget is allocated for workshops, consultations and stakeholder engagement. Approved consultant travel costs to Sudan, where travel is required and approved, will be handled separately through the operational provision. Importantly, travel to Sudan is subject to security assessments . The methodology also anticipates hybrid engagement arrangements combining remote and in-person consultations, reflecting the prevailing security context. Methodology Expected from the Consultant The successful consultant or firm is expected to use a methodology appropriate for complex policy and institutional reform. The British Council specifically expects: A co-creation and participatory approach ; A systems approach linking policy, institutions and implementation; Use of international best practices , including relevant ILO and UNESCO approaches and comparative RPL models; and Hybrid engagement modalities , incorporating remote and in-person consultation where appropriate. Applicants preparing their technical proposals should therefore pay close attention to these methodological expectations. The proposal should demonstrate not only what the applicant intends to deliver but also how the consultant or team will engage stakeholders, translate international experience into the Sudanese context and develop an implementable national framework. Reporting and Management Arrangements The selected consultant or consultancy firm will report to the Youth Skills Programme Manager, British Council Sudan . Technical coordination will also be maintained with relevant government stakeholders. The British Council will be responsible for overall contract management and logistical support associated with consultations. This arrangement means the consultant will need to operate effectively across technical, governmental and programme-management environments. Required Expertise and Experience Applicants should demonstrate strong and directly relevant expertise. The British Council requires proven experience in designing and implementing Recognition of Prior Learning systems or frameworks . Applicants should also demonstrate strong expertise in: Technical and Vocational Education and Training systems reform; Qualifications frameworks; Skills recognition; Non-formal education systems; and Related policy and institutional development. Experience working in fragile or conflict-affected contexts is another important requirement. Applicants should be capable of facilitating complex multi-stakeholder policy processes , given the significant consultation and co-creation responsibilities involved in the assignment. Familiarity with ILO, UNESCO or other international RPL standards is described as highly desirable. Additional Considerations for Consultancy Firms Consultancy firms interested in applying should consider the multidisciplinary nature of the assignment. For firms, a multidisciplinary team covering policy, assessment and institutional design is preferred . A strong team proposal should therefore demonstrate how the combined expertise of key personnel addresses the different technical components of the assignment. Application Requirements Interested individual consultants and consultancy firms are expected to submit several important documents. Applicants should prepare: Technical Proposal – explaining the proposed methodology and approach for undertaking the assignment. Financial Proposal – providing the financial proposal for delivering the consultancy. Relevant Experience and References – demonstrating previous experience related to the requirements of the assignment. CV(s) of Key Personnel – outlining the qualifications and professional experience of the consultant or proposed team members. The vacancy notice particularly emphasises that applicants should attach the technical proposal for developing the RPL Policy Framework together with their CV . Applicants should therefore carefully review the Terms of Reference and ensure their technical proposal addresses the assignment s expected methodology, scope, stakeholder engagement requirements, deliverables and implementation considerations. APPLY NOW Ethical Requirements The selected consultant or consultancy firm must comply with important ethical principles throughout the assignment. These include adherence to: Do no harm principles ; and Data protection and confidentiality standards . These requirements are especially significant considering the sensitive operating environment and the range of government, civil society, education-sector and development stakeholders expected to participate in the process. British Council RPL Consultant Application Deadline The closing date for applications is 26 August 2026 . Applicants should ensure that all required documents are prepared and submitted through the British Council recruitment system before the closing date. Application Deadline: 26 August 2026 Because the application requires more than a CV, prospective applicants should allow sufficient time to prepare a strong technical proposal, financial proposal, evidence of relevant experience, references and CVs for relevant personnel. Important Points Applicants Should Remember Before applying for the British Council International Consultant – Recognition of Prior Learning opportunity, prospective applicants should take note of the following: The consultancy focuses on developing a National Recognition of Prior Learning Policy Framework for Sudan . The assignment requires substantial expertise in RPL systems and frameworks. Strong knowledge of TVET reform, qualifications frameworks, skills recognition and non-formal education is required. Experience in fragile or conflict-affected environments is expected. Applicants must be able to facilitate multi-stakeholder policy processes. Familiarity with ILO, UNESCO or international RPL standards is highly desirable. Consultancy firms preferably should propose multidisciplinary expertise covering policy, assessment and institutional design. The work involves policy development as well as practical implementation guidance. Stakeholder engagement and co-creation are central components of the assignment. The contract is expected to continue until 31 March 2027 . The estimated level of effort is up to 42 working days across the contract period. Engagement may involve both remote and in-person activities. Travel to Sudan, where approved, is subject to security assessments. Applicants must submit a technical proposal. A financial proposal is required. Relevant experience and references must be provided. CVs of key personnel must be submitted. The application deadline is 26 August 2026 . Conclusion The British Council International Consultant – Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) opportunity in Sudan provides experienced education, TVET, qualifications and policy specialists with an opportunity to contribute to an important national skills-system initiative. At the centre of the consultancy is the challenge of developing a Recognition of Prior Learning system capable of acknowledging competencies acquired through non-formal and informal pathways and connecting those competencies more effectively with recognised qualifications, education and employment opportunities. The assignment is particularly significant within Sudan s current context, where conflict, displacement, disrupted education and the dominance of informal economic activity have increased the importance of flexible and inclusive approaches to skills recognition. The successful consultant or consultancy firm will be expected to move beyond producing a high-level policy document. The work encompasses policy and legal considerations, institutional architecture, governance, competency assessment, certification, quality assurance, implementation guidance, stakeholder co-creation and support for final validation and endorsement.
