title: RMIT University Research Fellow 2026: Apply for the Technology Adoption & Social Change Position in Melbourne, Australia
summary: RMIT University is inviting applications for an exciting Research Fellow in Technology Adoption Social Change position based in Melbourne, Australia. This four-year, full-time research appointment offers an opportunity for an appropriately qualified social sciences researcher to contribute to multidisciplinary research examining how people, workplaces and communities interact with emerging sensing technologies, artificial intelligence and complex data environments. The successful applicant will join the Technology Adoption and Social Change (TASC) program within the ARC Industrial Transformation Research Hub for Intelligent Contaminant-Sensing in Complex Environments (IC-SensE) . The position brings together social science, technology, artificial intelligence, industry collaboration and human-centred research, making it particularly relevant to researchers interested in the societal implications of emerging technologies. Based primarily at RMIT University s Melbourne CBD campus , the Research Fellow will conduct and contribute to high-quality research exploring consumer and workforce adoption of sensor technologies. The researcher will work alongside multidisciplinary academics and industry partners while investigating issues including socially responsible technology design, user experience, data security, trustworthy representation of data and AI-enabled workplace practices. Applications for the RMIT University Research Fellow position close on 15 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. About the RMIT University Research Fellow Position The Research Fellow, Technology Adoption Social Change position is a full-time, fixed-term appointment for four years . The successful candidate will be situated within RMIT University s School of Global, Urban and Social Studies , which forms part of the University s College of Design and Social Context. The Research Fellow will also have an affiliation with RMIT s Centre for Human-AI Information Environments . This institutional setting provides an interdisciplinary environment in which the successful researcher can contribute social science expertise to research involving technological innovation, artificial intelligence, sensing systems, workplaces, consumers and society. Key employment details include: Position: Research Fellow, Technology Adoption Social Change Institution: RMIT University Program: Technology Adoption and Social Change (TASC) Research Hub: ARC Industrial Transformation Research Hub for Intelligent Contaminant-Sensing in Complex Environments (IC-SensE) Location: Melbourne, Victoria, Australia Primary campus: Melbourne CBD campus Employment type: Full-time Contract: Fixed term for four years Academic classification: Academic Level B Superannuation: 17% Working arrangements: Flexible working arrangements are available Application deadline: 15 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. RMIT job requisition number: JR49996 Although the role is based at RMIT s Melbourne CBD campus, the successful candidate may be required to work at or be based at other RMIT University campuses when necessary. What Is the Technology Adoption and Social Change Program? The Technology Adoption and Social Change (TASC) program is part of the broader IC-SensE research initiative. TASC investigates how consumers and workers adopt and experience sensing technologies, with particular attention to the human and social dimensions of technological change. Rather than examining sensing technologies exclusively from an engineering or technical perspective, the program uses human-centred social research methodologies to understand what happens when technologies enter workplaces, industries and people s everyday experiences. The program therefore addresses questions surrounding the relationship between technological innovation and society. Areas examined through the program include: Consumer adoption of sensor technologies Workforce adoption of emerging technologies Human-centred technology implementation Socially responsible technology design User experiences of sensing technologies Data security Trust in technology and data Trustworthy representation of data Artificial intelligence in workplaces AI-enabled work practices Social implications of technological adoption Interactions between technology, workers, consumers and organisations The Research Fellow will play an important role in developing research that can help researchers, industries and other stakeholders understand these issues. About the ARC Research Hub IC-SensE The ARC Industrial Transformation Research Hub for Intelligent Contaminant-Sensing in Complex Environments (IC-SensE) is a multidisciplinary research initiative focused on developing human-focused sensing technologies integrated with artificial intelligence. IC-SensE received $4.75 million in funding through the 2025 round of the ARC Industrial Transformation Research Program scheme . The Hub focuses on technologies capable of supporting the real-time assessment of contaminants and helping predict potential hazards before they occur. This means its work extends beyond simply detecting contaminants. By combining sensing technologies with artificial intelligence, researchers aim to create systems capable of generating timely information that could help anticipate and manage potential risks. At the same time, IC-SensE recognises that successful technology development and deployment involves more than technical capability. New sensing and AI technologies ultimately interact with people, workplaces, organisations and communities. Questions surrounding trust, adoption, usability, security, ethics, social responsibility and workplace practices can therefore become central to whether new technologies achieve meaningful impact. This is where the TASC program and the Research Fellow position become particularly important. Learn more at https://icsensehub.org.au/ A Multidisciplinary Research Environment IC-SensE brings together researchers from Australian and international universities alongside industry leaders. Participating researchers represent fields including: Engineering Computer science Health Built environment Social science Industry engagement spans areas such as: Health and medical devices Artificial intelligence Environmental industries Energy Software development Defence Within this broad interdisciplinary environment, the TASC team contributes social science expertise and examines the human and social implications of sensing technologies across different contexts. The team is led by social scientists who collaborate across disciplinary boundaries to understand workplace and consumer experiences of technology adoption. For the successful Research Fellow, this creates an opportunity to conduct social science research while collaborating with experts working across technology, AI, engineering, health and other disciplines. What Will the Research Fellow Do? The successful candidate will lead and contribute to high-quality research within the Technology Adoption and Social Change program. An important component of the position involves examining the adoption of sensor technologies from a human-centred perspective using social research methodologies. The Research Fellow will work collaboratively with researchers from different academic disciplines as well as industry partners. Research areas may include: Socially Responsible Design The researcher may examine how sensing technologies can be designed and introduced in ways that recognise social needs, responsibilities and consequences. User Experience Understanding how workers, consumers and other users interact with technologies is central to successful adoption. The Research Fellow may investigate people s experiences, expectations, concerns and responses when engaging with sensing systems. Data Security Sensor technologies can generate significant amounts of information. Research within the program can therefore involve questions surrounding the security and responsible management of data. Trustworthy Data Representation Producing data is only one part of a technological system. People also need to understand and appropriately interpret information generated by technologies. The Research Fellow will contribute to research concerning trustworthy ways of representing and communicating data. AI-Enabled Work Practices As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into workplaces, researchers need to understand how it affects workers, organisations and established professional practices. The TASC program provides an environment for examining these changing relationships between people, AI and work. Research Outputs and Academic Responsibilities The Research Fellow will be expected to contribute to RMIT s broader research performance. The successful candidate will develop productive research networks and generate high-quality research outputs. Responsibilities are expected to include activities such as: Conducting high-quality academic research Developing new research initiatives Producing scholarly research outputs Contributing to publications Building productive academic and professional research networks Working with multidisciplinary researchers Collaborating with industry partners Applying for competitive research funding Managing research projects Translating research findings for different audiences Contributing to policy and practice Engaging government, industry and community stakeholders Supporting research with economic, environmental and societal relevance Potentially engaging, collaborating with and/or supervising higher degree by research candidates The position therefore combines independent research with teamwork, stakeholder engagement, research translation and academic collaboration. Research With Practical Economic, Environmental and Societal Impact One of the notable aspects of the position is its emphasis on translating academic findings into accessible and actionable outcomes. The successful applicant will not only be expected to produce academic research but also to consider how research findings can generate wider value. IC-SensE aims to ensure that its projects benefit participating universities and industry partners while creating broader impacts for: The economy The environment Society This makes research translation an important element of the Research Fellow s responsibilities. Applicants with experience communicating research beyond traditional academic audiences may therefore find this aspect of the role particularly relevant. Mandatory Academic Qualification RMIT University identifies one mandatory academic requirement for the position: Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent qualification in a relevant social sciences research field. Candidates who do not meet this mandatory requirement should carefully review the official position description before applying. Because the program examines technological adoption from a social and human-centred perspective, the position requires strong social science research expertise rather than solely technical expertise in sensing technologies or artificial intelligence. Research Experience and Track Record Required Successful applicants should demonstrate an emerging track record and recognition for producing quality research outputs capable of contributing to RMIT s existing high-performing research teams. Evidence may include: Academic publications Development of new research initiatives Participation in competitive research funding Contributions to policy Contributions to professional or organisational practice Other evidence demonstrating research quality and impact The wording of the position indicates that RMIT is looking for someone capable of contributing meaningfully to established research teams while continuing to develop their own research profile. Qualitative and Social Research Methodology Experience Applicants should have demonstrated experience designing and conducting qualitative research . The role particularly emphasises interdisciplinarity and social sciences methodologies aligned with the work of the IC-SensE Hub. Relevant methodological experience may include: Qualitative research Participatory research methods Mixed-methods research Other relevant social research methodologies Applicants should clearly demonstrate their methodological capabilities when addressing the Key Selection Criteria. Where possible, candidates should provide concrete examples of previous research projects, their methodological responsibilities, the research questions addressed and the resulting outputs or impact. Industry, Government and Community Engagement The position is not limited to university-based research. RMIT is seeking candidates with experience engaging with industry, government or community stakeholders through collaborative research projects and/or research translation activities. Applicants should therefore consider highlighting previous experience involving: Industry research partnerships Government collaboration Community-based research Research translation Stakeholder consultation Collaborative research projects Policy engagement Knowledge exchange Projects designed to create societal impact The ability to communicate effectively with people outside the candidate s immediate academic discipline is particularly valuable in a multidisciplinary research hub. Independent and Collaborative Working Skills The successful applicant must be capable of working independently while also contributing effectively to teams. The position requires someone who can: Manage independent research responsibilities Lead teams when required Collaborate across academic disciplines Build relationships with researchers Engage external stakeholders Work constructively within multidisciplinary project environments This balance is particularly important because IC-SensE incorporates researchers from several academic fields and collaborates with multiple industry sectors. Competitive Research Funding Experience Candidates should have experience applying for competitive research funding and successfully managing research projects . Applicants preparing their application may therefore want to provide specific evidence of involvement in: Grant applications Research funding proposals Funded research projects Project planning Research project management Budget or resource management, where relevant Delivery of project milestones Reporting and research outputs Applicants do not necessarily need to restrict examples to projects for which they were the sole lead researcher. Where appropriate, they can clearly explain their individual contribution to collaborative applications and funded research projects. Communication and Interpersonal Skills Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities are essential for the Research Fellow position. RMIT specifically seeks candidates capable of confidently and effectively working with: Academic colleagues Project team leaders Industry stakeholders Community stakeholders Government stakeholders Higher degree by research candidates Strong scholarly communication practices are also required. The successful applicant may be expected to communicate complex research findings to audiences with different levels of technical and academic expertise. Opportunity to Work at the Intersection of Social Science and Artificial Intelligence One particularly interesting feature of this position is the opportunity to contribute to research at the intersection of social science, sensing technology and artificial intelligence . The Research Fellow will be affiliated with RMIT s Centre for Human-AI Information Environments , in addition to being based within the School of Global, Urban and Social Studies. This provides an environment for examining not only whether technologies function effectively, but how people understand, trust, adopt and experience them. For researchers interested in the social dimensions of AI, human-centred technology, responsible innovation and changing workplace practices, the position offers a substantial four-year research appointment within an interdisciplinary program. Salary, Superannuation and Working Arrangements The Research Fellow position is classified at Academic Level B . In addition to the applicable Academic Level B salary, the successful candidate will receive 17% superannuation . RMIT also states that flexible working arrangements are available. Applicants should consult the official RMIT vacancy and associated position description for complete employment conditions and the applicable salary information. Location: Melbourne, Australia The position is primarily based at RMIT University s Melbourne CBD campus in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia . However, RMIT notes that the successful candidate may be required to work and/or be based at other University campuses. Applicants considering relocation should independently investigate practical matters such as Australian work rights, immigration requirements, accommodation and relocation costs where relevant. The supplied vacancy information does not state that visa sponsorship or relocation assistance is provided, so applicants should not assume that either benefit is available unless confirmed directly by RMIT. Pre-Employment Checks Appointment to the position is subject to required background screening. RMIT states that appointment is subject to passing: A Working with Children Check A National Police Check From 1 January 2026, RMIT also considers gender-based violence risk factors as part of its recruitment processes. Applicants are required to complete a gender-based violence declaration in accordance with the National Higher Education Code to Prevent and Respond to Gender-based Violence . Preferred candidates will also be required to undertake relevant pre-employment background checks. RMIT University s Equal Opportunity Commitment RMIT describes itself as an equal opportunity employer and a child-safe organisation. The University states that it is committed to attracting, retaining and developing people regardless of: Gender identity Ethnicity Sexual orientation Disability Age Applications are encouraged from all sectors of the community, with RMIT particularly encouraging applications from the Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander community . RMIT also actively supports and encourages people with disability to apply and provides support for adjustments throughout recruitment, selection and employment. Candidates requiring adjustments during the recruitment process can contact RMIT s talent support service using the contact information provided on the official vacancy. RMIT is also a Circle Back Initiative Employer , meaning it commits to responding to every applicant. How to Apply for the RMIT Research Fellow Position Applications must be submitted through the official RMIT University recruitment system. Candidates are instructed to submit: Curriculum Vitae (CV) Covering letter addressing the Key Selection Criteria Applicants should pay particular attention to the requirement to address the Key Selection Criteria. Rather than submitting a generic cover letter, candidates should use their application to demonstrate how their qualifications, research experience, methodological expertise, funding experience, stakeholder engagement and communication abilities correspond to the requirements of the position. Where appropriate, applicants can support their claims with specific examples from previous research projects. APPLY NOW What Should Applicants Highlight in Their Cover Letter? Because RMIT specifically requests a covering letter addressing the Key Selection Criteria, candidates should ensure their application provides clear evidence of their suitability. Depending on their experience, applicants may want to address: Their PhD or equivalent qualification in a relevant social sciences field Their research specialisation Their publication record Their experience developing new research initiatives Their qualitative research expertise Their experience with participatory and/or mixed-methods research Their ability to work across disciplines Their experience working with industry, government or community stakeholders Their involvement in research translation Their experience applying for competitive research funding Their research project management experience Their ability to work independently Their experience leading or contributing to research teams Their scholarly communication skills Their ability to communicate with non-academic stakeholders Their experience engaging with or supervising higher degree research candidates, where applicable Examples of research contributing to policy, practice or societal impact Applicants should ensure that all statements are accurate and supported by their actual experience. Application Deadline The deadline for applications is: 15 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Prospective candidates should aim to submit their application well before the deadline to allow sufficient time to complete the online application, upload the required documents and address the Key Selection Criteria thoroughly. Applications should be made through RMIT University s official careers portal. Further Information and Contact Candidates who require further information about the position can contact: Lisa Given Enabling Impact Platform Director, Social Change RMIT University Email: lisa.given2@rmit.edu.au Applicants should also review the official Research Fellow Position Description available through the RMIT University vacancy page before applying. Additional information about the IC-SensE Research Hub is available through the Hub s official website. Why This Research Position Is Significant The RMIT University Research Fellow in Technology Adoption Social Change position provides an opportunity to investigate one of the increasingly important questions surrounding technological innovation: how emerging technologies interact with people and society . Sensor systems and artificial intelligence can offer substantial technical capabilities, but successful adoption depends on more than technological performance. Workers and consumers need to understand technologies. Organisations must consider responsible implementation. Data must be managed and represented appropriately. Users need to determine whether systems are trustworthy. Workplaces must adapt to new AI-enabled practices. These human and social questions sit at the heart of the TASC program. For an appropriately qualified social sciences researcher, the four-year appointment offers an opportunity to investigate these issues while participating in a multidisciplinary ARC-funded research environment connecting universities and industry. Conclusion Applications are now invited for the RMIT University Research Fellow, Technology Adoption Social Change, ARC Research Hub IC-SensE position in Melbourne, Australia . The successful candidate will join a multidisciplinary research environment focused on the intersection of sensing technology, artificial intelligence, social research and human-centred technology adoption. Working within the Technology Adoption and Social Change program, the Research Fellow will contribute to research concerning socially responsible design, user experience, data security, trustworthy data representation, AI-enabled work practices and the broader societal implications of emerging sensing technologies. Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent in a relevant social sciences research field and should demonstrate strong qualitative and social research capabilities, an emerging record of quality research outputs, experience with research funding and project management, stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to work effectively across disciplinary boundaries. title: University of British Columbia Four Year Doctoral Fellowship 2026: Fully Funded PhD Opportunity for International and Canadian Students
summary: The University of British Columbia (UBC) Four Year Doctoral Fellowship (4YF) is a major doctoral funding opportunity designed to support outstanding students undertaking advanced research at one of Canada s leading universities. The fellowship provides substantial financial support to eligible doctoral students, including international students, Canadian citizens, and permanent residents. Effective September 2026 onward , recipients of the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship can receive a $24,000 annual stipend plus full tuition coverage per year for up to four years of their doctoral studies. The Four Year Doctoral Fellowship program is intended to help UBC attract and retain exceptional doctoral researchers while giving recipients stable base-level financial support for their studies and research. One particularly important feature of the 4YF is its application process. Students do not normally submit a separate application specifically for the fellowship. Instead, PhD, DMA, and MDPhD applicants who are offered admission to UBC are automatically considered for 4YF funding . For prospective doctoral students searching for UBC scholarships for international students, fully funded PhD opportunities in Canada, doctoral scholarships in Canada, UBC PhD funding, or Canadian scholarships for international doctoral students , the Four Year Doctoral Fellowship is an important funding opportunity to consider. UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship 2026 Overview Here are the major details prospective applicants should know: Host institution: The University of British Columbia (UBC) Campus: Vancouver Campus, Canada Program: Four Year Doctoral Fellowship (4YF) Degree level: Doctoral Eligible doctoral programs: PhD, DMA, and MDPhD Annual stipend: $24,000 Tuition: Full tuition coverage Maximum funding period: Up to four years Citizenship eligibility: Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and international students Selection basis: Academic excellence and recommendation by the graduate program Application method: Apply for admission to an appropriate UBC graduate program Separate 4YF application: Generally not required for incoming applicants Deadline: Set individually by each UBC graduate program New funding level effective: September 2026 onward What Is the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship? The Four Year Doctoral Fellowship , commonly referred to as the 4YF , is a funding program established by the University of British Columbia to support high-achieving doctoral students. Doctoral education can require several years of intensive academic study, original research, laboratory or fieldwork, data collection, academic writing, and dissertation preparation. Stable funding can therefore be an important factor in allowing doctoral researchers to concentrate on their academic work. Through the 4YF program, UBC provides selected doctoral students with a combination of stipend funding and tuition support. The university describes the program as a mechanism that allows UBC to continue attracting and supporting outstanding domestic and international doctoral students while providing recipients with stable, base-level funding for their doctoral studies and research. UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship Value Beginning September 2026 , the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship provides recipients with: $24,000 Annual Stipend Successful recipients can receive $24,000 in stipend funding per year . The stipend provides financial support while recipients undertake their doctoral studies and research. Full Tuition Coverage In addition to the $24,000 stipend, the fellowship provides tuition coverage . This makes the funding package particularly significant because the fellowship addresses both tuition expenses and provides a stipend. Funding for Up to Four Years The 4YF can provide funding for up to four years of doctoral study . However, applicants should understand that four years represents the potential maximum duration rather than a guarantee that every recipient will receive precisely four years of support. UBC states that the duration can be shorter in certain circumstances. Recipients should consult the official 4YF Guidelines for detailed policies governing the duration and administration of their funding. Funding is also subject to recipients maintaining satisfactory academic progress . How Much Could the UBC 4YF Be Worth Over Four Years? At the stated rate of $24,000 per year , a recipient funded at that stipend level for the full four years could receive up to $96,000 in stipend funding , in addition to applicable tuition coverage. The calculation is: $24,000 per year × 4 years = $96,000 in stipend funding The actual amount and duration received by an individual student can depend on their circumstances, funding period, other scholarships, academic standing, and the rules contained in UBC s Four Year Doctoral Fellowship Guidelines. Who Can Apply for the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship? The UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship is available to both domestic and international doctoral students . UBC states that Four Year Fellowships may be held by: Canadian students; Canadian permanent residents; and International students. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to international students seeking doctoral funding in Canada. There is no country-specific restriction stated in the supplied fellowship information. International students from different regions of the world may therefore be considered as long as they satisfy the relevant UBC doctoral admission requirements and other conditions of the program. Eligible Degree Programs The fellowship is generally offered to students beginning their first year of full-time study in one of the following types of doctoral programs: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) Combined MD/PhD (MDPhD) While incoming doctoral students are a major focus of the program, UBC states that Four Year Fellowships may also be offered to continuing students . Therefore, the fellowship is not necessarily restricted exclusively to new doctoral students. Priority for Incoming Doctoral Students Each UBC graduate program receives an allocation of Four Year Fellowships. Graduate programs assess their incoming and continuing doctoral students and select their strongest candidates for the available fellowships. According to UBC, priority is given to incoming students . Prospective doctoral candidates with excellent academic records should therefore pay particular attention to the admission requirements and deadlines of their intended graduate program, because applying for admission is also the route through which incoming candidates are considered for 4YF funding. UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship Eligibility Requirements Although individual circumstances can vary, the major eligibility considerations include the following. 1. Applicants Should Be Pursuing an Eligible Doctoral Program The fellowship is generally intended for full-time students in PhD, DMA, or MDPhD programs. 2. Domestic and International Students Are Eligible The fellowship is not restricted to Canadian citizens. Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and international students can hold Four Year Fellowships. 3. Academic Excellence Is Essential UBC states that selection is based on academic excellence , following a recommendation from the student s graduate program. This means admission to a doctoral program does not automatically guarantee receipt of the fellowship. 4. Incoming Students Receive Priority Although continuing students may receive a 4YF, graduate programs give priority to incoming students when selecting recipients. 5. Recipients Must Maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress Continued funding is subject to satisfactory academic progress. Students who receive the fellowship should therefore familiarize themselves with the academic and administrative conditions attached to the award. Selection and Evaluation Criteria Selection for the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship is based on academic excellence . Recommendations are made through individual graduate programs. This means that the relevant graduate program plays an important role in identifying and recommending candidates for the fellowship. Because the number of fellowships allocated to each graduate program is limited, applicants should understand that simply satisfying UBC s minimum doctoral admission requirements does not necessarily mean they will receive a Four Year Fellowship. Graduate programs review eligible students and offer fellowships to their strongest candidates. How to Apply for the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship The application process is relatively straightforward for prospective doctoral students because there is generally no separate 4YF application required from incoming applicants . Step 1: Identify an Appropriate UBC Graduate Program Prospective students should first identify a PhD, DMA, or MDPhD program at the University of British Columbia that aligns with their academic background and research interests. Students planning a research degree may also wish to investigate potential faculty supervisors whose research interests correspond with their proposed area of study. Step 2: Review the Graduate Program s Admission Requirements Admission requirements can vary between UBC graduate programs. Applicants should carefully review the requirements of the particular program they intend to enter, including academic qualifications, supporting documents, research requirements, language requirements where applicable, and any program-specific conditions. Step 3: Check the Program-Specific Application Deadline This step is especially important because there is no single university-wide 4YF deadline listed for applicants . The deadline is set by each UBC graduate program . Applicants must therefore check the application deadline for their chosen graduate program and ensure their admission application is submitted on time. Step 4: Apply for Admission to UBC To be considered for Four Year Fellowship funding, prospective students submit an application for admission to the appropriate UBC graduate program. Step 5: Automatic Consideration for 4YF Funding All PhD, DMA, and MDPhD applicants who are offered admission are automatically considered for Four Year Fellowship funding . This means applicants generally do not need to prepare and submit an additional standalone application for the 4YF itself. Step 6: Graduate Programs Select Their Strongest Candidates Each graduate program receives an allocation of Four Year Fellowships and reviews incoming and continuing students. The programs then offer the fellowships to their strongest candidates, with priority given to incoming students. For information about admission procedures and requirements visit the Application Admission page. APPLY NOW UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship Deadline There is no single deadline for the Four Year Doctoral Fellowship . Deadline: Set by each UBC graduate program. Prospective applicants should not interpret the absence of a universal deadline as meaning that applications can be submitted at any time. Instead, applicants must check the admission deadline for the specific doctoral program to which they wish to apply. Since admission to an eligible graduate program is the route through which incoming students are considered for 4YF funding, missing the relevant graduate admission deadline could also mean missing the opportunity to be considered for the fellowship for that admission cycle. Applicants should therefore verify the current deadline directly through UBC s official graduate program and admission pages. Nomination Process The nomination process is primarily handled internally by UBC graduate programs rather than by applicants themselves. Each graduate program receives a certain number of Four Year Fellowships each year. Programs review both incoming and continuing students and select their strongest students, with incoming students receiving priority. After selecting a recipient, the graduate program notifies UBC Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies by submitting a signed University Award Recommendation Form . For administrative purposes, the program uses award number 6456 . UBC states that it is not necessary to list an award amount on the recommendation form. Recommendation forms should be submitted at least eight weeks before the requested 4YF start date . This eight-week timeframe concerns the university s nomination/recommendation process and should not be confused with the student s graduate admission deadline. Tri-Agency Award Holders and the 4YF The Four Year Doctoral Fellowship also interacts with several major Canadian research awards. Students holding certain Tri-Agency awards automatically become 4YF designates . These include: Vanier Scholarships; Doctoral Canada Graduate Scholarships (CGSD); Canadian Institutes of Health Research Doctoral Research Awards; Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council Doctoral Postgraduate Scholarships (PGSD); and Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council Doctoral Fellowships. Doctoral students who receive qualifying Tri-Agency scholarships may be eligible for 4YF tuition coverage . They can also receive 4YF stipend and tuition support after their external scholarship funding ends, subject to the applicable time limits. According to the information provided by UBC, this support can continue until four years after the external award start date or until the end of the student s fifth year in the doctoral program, whichever occurs first . Other Major External Scholarship Winners The 4YF can also interact with other major external scholarships. Recipients of major external scholarships who are selected as 4YF designates may be eligible for tuition coverage through the 4YF. They may subsequently receive 4YF stipend and tuition support after their external scholarship funding concludes. For these recipients, funding can continue until four years after the 4YF start date or until the end of their fifth year in the doctoral program, whichever occurs first . Students receiving external funding should carefully review UBC s official 4YF Guidelines to understand how their external scholarship interacts with their Four Year Fellowship designation. Important Funding Requirement for 4YF Holders Receiving a Four Year Doctoral Fellowship does not necessarily mean students can ignore other external funding opportunities. UBC requires 4YF holders to apply for other funding in order to maintain their eligibility for 4YF funding . The requirements differ depending on the student s status. Canadian Citizens and Permanent Residents 4YF holders who are Canadian citizens or permanent residents must apply for Tri-Agency funding every year when eligible . This is an important condition. UBC states that eligible Canadian citizens or permanent residents who fail to apply for the required Tri-Agency funding will forfeit their remaining 4YF funding . Recipients should therefore take this requirement seriously and keep track of relevant external scholarship competitions and deadlines. International Students International 4YF recipients are not required to apply to the annual Affiliated Fellowship competition, which is held each fall. However, international recipients are eligible to enter the competition if they choose. Doing so may provide an opportunity to compete for Affiliated Fellowships carrying higher stipend amounts, including opportunities such as the Killam Doctoral Fellowship . Can 4YF Funding Be Interrupted? UBC provides a mechanism through which 4YF payments can be interrupted for certain non-academic reasons. Examples given by the university include: Relevant work experience; and Paid internships. UBC provides a 4YF Interruption Form for recipients who need such an interruption and who do not intend to apply for a corresponding professional leave of absence from the university. Because interruptions can affect fellowship payments and potentially the administration of an award, recipients considering this option should consult UBC s official rules and relevant graduate program before making arrangements. Why the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship Is an Important Opportunity The UBC 4YF stands out because it combines several significant benefits. Substantial Annual Financial Support A $24,000 annual stipend provides recipients with a meaningful base level of financial support during their doctoral studies. Tuition Coverage The fellowship also provides tuition coverage, reducing one of the major educational costs associated with completing a doctoral degree. Potential Four-Year Duration Funding may be available for up to four years, providing a degree of financial stability over a substantial portion of a recipient s doctoral studies. International Students Are Eligible International students can be considered alongside Canadian citizens and permanent residents, making the fellowship relevant to doctoral candidates worldwide. No Separate Fellowship Application for Incoming Applicants Eligible PhD, DMA, and MDPhD applicants who receive an offer of admission are automatically considered for 4YF funding. This reduces the need to complete a separate fellowship application during the initial admission process. Broad Research Possibilities at UBC The examples of current and previous award holders provided by UBC illustrate the breadth of research supported through doctoral study at the university. Research represented among featured fellowship holders includes areas such as: Microbiology and immunology; Interdisciplinary studies; Zoology; Biochemistry and molecular biology; Oceanography; Population and public health; Gender, race, sexuality and social justice; School and applied child psychology; Resources, environment and sustainability; and Cell and developmental biology. These examples demonstrate that the Four Year Doctoral Fellowship is not confined to one narrow academic discipline. Important Points Applicants Should Remember Prospective applicants should keep several important details in mind: Apply for admission first. Incoming applicants are considered for the 4YF through their application to an eligible UBC doctoral program. There is no universal deadline. The deadline is determined by each graduate program, so applicants need to check the deadline for their chosen program. Admission does not guarantee a fellowship. Applicants offered admission are automatically considered, but individual graduate programs select their strongest candidates from the eligible pool. Academic excellence is central to selection. The fellowship is intended to support outstanding doctoral students. Incoming students receive priority. Continuing students may receive a fellowship, but UBC states that priority is given to incoming students. International students are eligible. The program is open to international students as well as Canadian citizens and permanent residents. Funding can last up to four years. However, the actual funding period can be shorter depending on individual circumstances and the applicable 4YF policies. Academic progress matters. Fellowship funding remains subject to satisfactory academic progress. Other funding obligations may apply. In particular, eligible Canadian citizens and permanent residents holding a 4YF must apply annually for Tri-Agency funding to retain their remaining 4YF eligibility. Recipients should read the official 4YF Guidelines. Detailed rules concerning the administration, duration, interruption, and interaction of 4YF funding with other awards are contained in UBC s official guidelines. Frequently Asked Questions About the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship Is the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship open to international students? Yes. UBC states that Four Year Fellowships can be held by both domestic and international students. How much is the UBC 4YF worth? Effective September 2026 onward, recipients receive $24,000 in stipend funding plus tuition per year , potentially for up to four years. Does the UBC 4YF cover tuition? Yes. Tuition coverage is included in the fellowship funding package. How long does the fellowship last? Funding may be provided for up to four years , although the duration can be shorter in some circumstances. Do applicants need to submit a separate 4YF application? For incoming applicants, generally no. PhD, DMA, and MDPhD applicants who are offered admission are automatically considered for Four Year Fellowship funding. What is the deadline for the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship? There is no single fellowship deadline applicable to every applicant. The deadline is set by each UBC graduate program. Applicants should check the admission deadline of their intended graduate program. Are continuing doctoral students eligible? Yes. Although the fellowships are generally offered to students beginning their first year of full-time doctoral studies, UBC states that continuing students may also receive them. What degrees qualify for the fellowship? The fellowship is generally associated with full-time PhD, DMA, and MDPhD studies. Is the scholarship awarded automatically after admission? No. Applicants offered admission to eligible programs are automatically considered , but this does not mean every admitted student automatically receives funding. Graduate programs select their strongest candidates based on academic excellence and their available fellowship allocations. How Prospective Applicants Can Strengthen Their Position Because selection is based on academic excellence and graduate-program recommendation, prospective students should focus on submitting the strongest possible application for admission. Applicants should carefully demonstrate their academic preparation, research potential, relevant experience, and suitability for their proposed doctoral program wherever these elements are requested as part of the admission process. For research-focused degrees, identifying appropriate faculty expertise and understanding the research environment of the intended graduate program can also be an important part of preparing a competitive doctoral application. Applicants should always follow the specific instructions issued by their chosen UBC program because requirements can vary across departments and disciplines. Final Reminder About the Deadline The UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship does not have one universal application deadline . Deadline: Set by each UBC graduate program. Prospective students should locate their intended PhD, DMA, or MDPhD program on UBC s official graduate website, confirm its current admission deadline, and submit all required admission materials according to that program s instructions. Applicants should avoid relying on deadlines associated with unrelated UBC programs because different graduate programs may operate according to different application schedules. Conclusion The University of British Columbia Four Year Doctoral Fellowship (4YF) represents a significant funding opportunity for outstanding students seeking doctoral education in Canada. With $24,000 in annual stipend funding plus tuition coverage for up to four years , the fellowship can provide recipients with substantial financial support while they pursue advanced research at UBC. Its accessibility to Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and international students makes the program particularly noteworthy for prospective doctoral candidates worldwide. Moreover, eligible PhD, DMA, and MDPhD applicants who are offered admission are automatically considered for the fellowship, meaning there is generally no separate 4YF application for incoming students. Competition should nevertheless be expected. Fellowships are allocated among UBC graduate programs, and programs select their strongest students based on academic excellence, with priority given to incoming candidates. Anyone interested in the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship 2026 should begin by identifying an appropriate UBC doctoral program, carefully reviewing its admission requirements, checking its specific application deadline, and preparing a strong application for admission. Most importantly, prospective applicants should remember that the deadline is determined by each UBC graduate program . Applicants should therefore consult the official University of British Columbia Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies website and their chosen graduate program for the latest admission requirements, deadlines, funding policies, and Four Year Doctoral Fellowship guidelines before applying. Visit the OFY website for more Fellowship Opportunities . title: COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon 2026 in Türkiye: Apply to Develop Climate Solutions and Join the International COP31 Ideathon in Antalya
summary: The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon is inviting young people across Türkiye to turn their climate ideas into practical solutions for some of the most urgent environmental challenges facing communities and the planet. Organized under the Turkish Ministry of Youth and Sports , the initiative provides young participants with an intensive opportunity to work in multidisciplinary teams, receive guidance from expert mentors, develop solutions to real environmental problems and present their ideas before a jury. The programme is particularly designed for young people interested in climate change, sustainability, environmental protection, zero waste and the circular economy . Participants will spend three days working collaboratively on a selected climate-related challenge, with the strongest teams potentially advancing to an international ideathon in Antalya held alongside the COP31 process. The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon offers an opportunity not only to develop an innovative climate solution but also to connect with young people from different parts of Türkiye and, for successful teams, eventually collaborate with participants from countries around the world. About the COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon is a youth-focused climate innovation and solution-development initiative designed to give young people an active role in responding to climate change. Rather than simply discussing the environmental challenges facing society, participants are encouraged to identify problems and develop original, practical and feasible solutions . The programme brings together young people from different cities and disciplines and places them in collaborative teams. With support from expert mentors, participants will work through a three-day ideathon experience to transform their initial ideas into more developed solutions. The initiative is connected to the broader COP31 process , creating a potential pathway for successful youth teams to take their solutions to an international platform in Antalya. The programme s underlying message is that young people should not only be consulted about the climate crisis but should also have opportunities to design and develop solutions that can contribute to the future of environmental policy and action. What Is an Ideathon? An ideathon is an intensive, collaborative problem-solving event in which participants work together to develop innovative responses to a particular challenge. In the case of the COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon, participants will: Select or be assigned a climate-related theme. Work in multidisciplinary youth teams. Examine a real environmental problem. Generate and refine potential solutions. Receive guidance from expert mentors. Develop a feasible solution proposal. Present their idea to a jury. Compete for the opportunity to progress to the international stage. The format encourages participants to move beyond general awareness of climate change and focus on solutions that can realistically address environmental challenges . What Participants Can Expect Selected participants will take part in a three-day experience focused on climate solution development. Three Days of Collaborative Solution Development Participants will work with their teams for three days to address a real environmental problem. The experience is intended to strengthen practical skills such as: Problem identification Research Critical thinking Creative thinking Collaboration Communication Solution design Presentation Project development Teamwork Participants will have the opportunity to turn an initial concept into a more structured and potentially implementable climate solution. Expert Mentorship Participants will receive one-on-one support from expert mentors working in relevant fields. Mentors can help participants: Evaluate their ideas. Identify weaknesses in proposed solutions. Improve feasibility. Develop stronger approaches to environmental problems. Think about implementation. Prepare their final presentations. This mentorship component is particularly valuable because participants are not expected to develop their ideas entirely on their own. Presentation Before a Jury At the end of the ideathon experience, teams will have the opportunity to present their ideas to a jury. This gives participants practical experience in communicating an environmental solution to decision-makers and experts. Teams will need to demonstrate not only that their idea is innovative but also that it can potentially address a genuine environmental challenge. Youth Networking The initiative will bring together young people from different cities across Türkiye. Participants can therefore build connections with peers who share interests in: Climate action Sustainability Environmental protection Renewable energy Circular economy Climate leadership Green transition The multidisciplinary nature of the programme can also help participants discover perspectives and approaches outside their usual academic or professional areas. Opportunity to Participate in the International Ideathon in Antalya One of the most significant opportunities associated with the COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon is the possibility of progressing to the international stage. Teams that perform particularly well may have the opportunity to participate in the international ideathon in Antalya during the COP31 process. At the international ideathon, successful teams will have the opportunity to: Develop their ideas on an international scale. Work alongside young participants from different countries. Exchange ideas across national and cultural contexts. Further refine their proposed solutions. Present their work on an international platform. Contribute to discussions connected with global climate challenges. This creates a potential progression from a local or national youth ideathon to an international climate innovation experience. COP31 and the International Climate Context The initiative is connected to the COP31 process , giving the programme an important international climate-policy dimension. The United Nations Climate Change Conference, commonly known as COP, brings countries together to discuss international action on climate change. The COP31-related youth initiative seeks to create space for young people to contribute their own ideas and solutions to environmental challenges. For participants, this can provide valuable exposure to the broader climate policy and sustainability ecosystem. Eight Climate and Sustainability Themes Participants will develop ideas under one of eight thematic areas. These themes cover a broad range of environmental, social and economic dimensions of climate action. 1. Green Skills and Climate Literacy This theme focuses on strengthening the knowledge and skills people need to understand and respond to climate change. Potential ideas could address: Climate education Environmental awareness Green skills development Youth climate education Sustainability training Climate communication Environmental literacy Young people interested in education, training and awareness-raising may find this theme particularly relevant. 2. Youth Participation and Climate Leadership This theme focuses on increasing young people s involvement in climate action and environmental decision-making. Possible areas of interest include: Youth participation Climate leadership Youth-led environmental initiatives Climate advocacy Youth representation Community engagement Environmental policymaking The theme recognizes young people as active contributors to climate solutions rather than passive beneficiaries of environmental policies. 3. Adaptation and Resilience to Climate Change Climate change is already affecting communities and ecosystems, making adaptation and resilience increasingly important. Participants working on this theme may explore solutions related to: Climate adaptation Disaster preparedness Community resilience Climate risk management Resilient infrastructure Local adaptation strategies Protection of vulnerable communities The emphasis is on developing approaches that can help communities prepare for and respond to climate-related risks. 4. Air Pollution, Clean Air and the Green Transition Air pollution represents both an environmental and public-health challenge. This theme invites ideas addressing: Air quality Pollution reduction Clean transportation Clean energy Sustainable urban development Green technologies Low-carbon transition Participants can explore innovative ways to reduce pollution while supporting a broader transition toward more sustainable systems. 5. Combating Forest Fires, Drought and Water Stress This theme addresses environmental challenges that can become more severe as climate conditions change. Participants may develop solutions relating to: Forest-fire prevention Early warning systems Drought management Water conservation Water security Climate-resilient ecosystems Community preparedness The theme is particularly relevant to innovative approaches that help communities and ecosystems cope with increasing environmental pressures. 6. Agriculture and Food Security Climate change has significant implications for agriculture and food systems. Ideas under this theme could explore: Climate-smart agriculture Sustainable farming Food security Agricultural resilience Efficient water use Sustainable food systems Reducing environmental impacts of agriculture Participants can examine how food systems can become more resilient while contributing to environmental sustainability. 7. Renewable Energy and Carbon Footprint Reduction This theme focuses on the transition toward cleaner energy systems and reducing greenhouse-gas emissions. Potential areas include: Renewable energy Solar energy Energy efficiency Low-carbon technologies Carbon footprint reduction Clean energy access Sustainable consumption Participants with interests in engineering, technology, energy or environmental science may find this theme particularly suitable. 8. Youth-Friendly and Environmentally Friendly Sports Facilities The final theme connects climate action with sports and youth facilities. Participants may explore how sports facilities can become: More environmentally sustainable More energy efficient More accessible to young people Less carbon intensive More resource efficient Better integrated into sustainable communities This theme demonstrates that climate action can be incorporated into many aspects of everyday community life. Learn More Who Can Apply? The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon is aimed specifically at young people between 15 and 29 years old . Applicants should have an interest in at least one of the areas connected to the programme, including: Climate change Sustainability Environmental protection Zero waste Circular economy Applicants do not need to be described as climate experts. The initiative is designed to give young people an opportunity to develop ideas with the support of mentors and other participants. The multidisciplinary nature of the programme means that young people with different educational, professional and personal backgrounds may be able to contribute. Nationality and Geographic Eligibility The programme information states that young people will be selected from across Türkiye and that the in-person ideathon events will take place in cities across Türkiye. Therefore, this opportunity is primarily intended for young people in Türkiye , particularly those eligible to participate through the Turkish Ministry of Youth and Sports E-Genç platform. The information provided does not indicate that applicants from other countries can directly apply to the national ideathon stages. However, participants whose teams successfully advance may have the opportunity to take part in the international ideathon in Antalya , where they can work alongside participants from different countries. International participation therefore appears to be associated with the later stage of the programme rather than the initial national application. Where Will the Ideathon Take Place? The national ideathon is scheduled to take place in seven cities across Türkiye . Istanbul 4–6 September 2026 Rize 9–11 September 2026 Adana 18–20 September 2026 Konya 25–27 September 2026 Izmir 2–4 October 2026 Mardin 9–11 October 2026 Erzurum 16–18 October 2026 Applicants should pay close attention to the location and dates relevant to their participation. How to Apply Applications are submitted through the E-Genç Platform , the youth-focused digital platform associated with the Turkish Ministry of Youth and Sports. During the application process, applicants are expected to provide a short solution proposal addressing one of the eight programme themes. A strong proposal should focus on a specific environmental or climate challenge and present a solution that is: Original Practical Feasible Relevant to the selected theme Potentially useful to communities Capable of being developed further during the ideathon Applicants should avoid presenting only a general statement about climate change. The purpose of the application is to demonstrate an ability to identify a problem and begin thinking about a realistic solution. APPLY HERE! What Makes a Strong Solution Proposal? Although the programme emphasizes creativity and innovation, a successful idea should also demonstrate practical thinking. Applicants can strengthen their proposals by considering questions such as: What is the problem? Clearly identify the climate or environmental challenge. For example, instead of simply discussing water scarcity, identify a particular aspect of water stress affecting communities. Who is affected? Explain the people, communities, ecosystems or sectors affected by the problem. What is your proposed solution? Describe the core idea clearly and simply. Why is the solution different? Explain what makes the proposal innovative or different from existing approaches. Is it feasible? Consider whether the solution could realistically be implemented with available or potentially accessible resources. What impact could it create? Explain how the proposed solution could improve environmental, social or community outcomes. Multidisciplinary Teams The programme places particular importance on teams made up of young people from different disciplines . This approach recognizes that complex climate challenges rarely have a single solution or belong to one academic field. For example, a climate solution might benefit from combining: Environmental science Engineering Economics Technology Agriculture Communications Public policy Business Education Design Participants will therefore have opportunities to learn from people with different knowledge, skills and perspectives. From Idea to Implementation The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon is designed to take participants beyond simply generating ideas. The three-day experience allows teams to develop their proposals through: Problem identification. Idea generation. Team discussion. Expert mentoring. Solution refinement. Feasibility consideration. Presentation preparation. Jury evaluation. The strongest teams can then potentially take their ideas to the international stage in Antalya. This progression gives participants an opportunity to see how an initial concept can evolve into a more developed climate solution. Benefits of Participating The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon offers several potential benefits for young participants. Practical Climate Innovation Experience Participants gain hands-on experience developing solutions to real environmental challenges. Expert Mentorship One-on-one guidance provides participants with access to experienced professionals who can help improve their ideas. Networking Participants can establish relationships with young people from different cities and potentially, at the international stage, from different countries. Presentation Skills Presenting before a jury can strengthen participants ability to communicate complex ideas clearly and persuasively. Teamwork Participants gain experience collaborating with people from different disciplines and backgrounds. Exposure to International Climate Action Successful teams may have the opportunity to participate in an international ideathon connected with the COP31 process. Contribution to Environmental Policy and Action The programme encourages young people to develop ideas that could potentially contribute to future environmental policies and climate solutions. Why Young People Should Consider Applying Climate change presents complex challenges requiring innovation across multiple sectors. Young people are often among the most affected by long-term environmental changes, but they also bring new perspectives, technologies and approaches to solving these problems. The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon provides a structured environment where young people can turn those perspectives into practical proposals. The programme can be particularly valuable for young people interested in building experience in: Climate policy Environmental science Sustainability Renewable energy Circular economy Agriculture Environmental technology Climate leadership Public policy Green innovation Community development Application Deadline The information provided for the COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon does not state a specific application closing date . Applications are currently presented as open through the E-Genç Platform . Applicants should therefore check the official application portal for the current submission deadline and complete their applications as early as possible. The scheduled national ideathon events begin on 4 September 2026 in Istanbul , followed by events in Rize, Adana, Konya, Izmir, Mardin and Erzurum through October 2026. Organizing Institution The initiative is regulated by the: Turkish Ministry of Youth and Sports Address: Örnek Mahallesi, Oruç Reis Caddesi No:13, Altındağ, Ankara, Türkiye The Ministry operates the youth-focused platforms and programmes through which participants can access information and submit applications. Important Information for Applicants Before applying, candidates should: Confirm that they meet the 15–29 age requirement . Review the eight available climate themes. Select a theme that matches their interests and strengths. Develop a clear and practical climate solution. Prepare the requested short solution proposal. Submit the application through the E-Genç Platform. Check the application portal for the latest deadline and participation details. Consider the location and dates of the relevant ideathon event. Be prepared to collaborate in a multidisciplinary team. Be available for the full three-day ideathon experience if selected. Visit HERE to learn more about the COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon 2026 in Türkiye. Conclusion The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon provides young people in Türkiye with an opportunity to move from climate awareness to practical climate action. Through three days of intensive teamwork, expert mentorship and solution development, participants can explore real environmental challenges and transform their ideas into more feasible and impactful proposals. The programme covers eight major areas, ranging from climate literacy and youth leadership to renewable energy, agriculture, food security, water stress, air pollution, forest fires and sustainable sports facilities. This broad thematic scope means that young people with different interests and backgrounds can contribute to the climate solution-building process. One of the programme s most attractive features is the potential pathway to the international ideathon in Antalya . Teams that perform particularly well may have the opportunity to work with participants from countries around the world and develop their ideas within an international COP31-related environment. Young people aged 15 to 29 in Türkiye who are passionate about climate change, sustainability, environmental protection, zero waste or the circular economy should consider preparing a strong solution proposal and applying through the E-Genç Platform. Because the information provided does not specify a final application closing date, prospective applicants should consult the official platform promptly for the latest deadline and application requirements.
